note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: Mostly sound, with one medium validity hole. Verified the following. The start graph fails first at V3 for exactly the stated reason ('Value "hum_cutoff" cannot be evaluated: name 'hum_cutoff' is not defined'; V1 and V2 pass), and the fault (a deleted variable block still referenced by the filter) is realistic. The instruction plus the start graph are self-contained: it states every number the oracle uses (8 kHz, 500 Hz, peak 0.4 / RMS 0.283, ≤0.1 % of power below 200 Hz, dehummed.dat, float). It names the symptom without leaking the fault location or the value, and I found no hidden requirement. Repair/L1 fits the brief's definitions (5 functional blocks, single rate), and disjointness from the training specs holds. No valid alternative was wrongly rejected: a parameter block instead of a variable, an added Throttle, an IIR Butterworth via scipy (iir_filter_xxx, oldstyle False), cutoffs 120/200/400 with width 100, and cutoff 100 with width 50 all pass V6. Designs that fail (cutoff 100-115 with width 100, cutoff 150 with width 200) really do violate the stated 0.1 % bound. Remaining problems: (F1, medium) answers that skip the repair entirely pass V6, because the oracle only sees the final output. These are tone-only (filter and hum source deleted, hum_cutoff never defined), anti-phase cancellation, and a zeroed hum with a wrong 60 Hz cutoff. The limitation is documented only in the build.py docstring, not in task.json. (F2, low) the cutoff pass boundary sits inside GRC's nominal stopband, and the docstring misstates why. (F3, low) the signature split lets this item's own correct variants (fir_filter_xxx, band_pass_filter) and a near-identical test item (gbf-test-05) fall into train or test, so template twins are not kept apart. Scratch candidates and runner: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-04/ (make_cands.py, run_cands.py, cands/*.grc). I did not modify the task directory.

findings.claim: The oracle accepts answers that never repair the fault and never filter anything. Two of the instruction's stated behaviours go unchecked: the flowgraph simulates a tone plus 60 Hz hum, and it filters the hum out. The only observation point is the final output, so any graph that writes a clean 500 Hz / 0.4 tone to dehummed.dat passes. That includes a graph that simply deletes the broken High Pass Filter (the block holding the undefined reference) together with the hum source.
findings.evidence: Ran ladder.check with the task's oracle on candidates in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-04/cands. (a) trivial_tone_only.grc: only samp_rate, the 500 Hz source and the File Sink. hum_cutoff is never defined and the filter is deleted. Result V6 pass (peak 500.0, rms 0.282843, max_abs 0.4, band_fraction 0.0). (b) cancel_antiphase.grc: HPF deleted, a third 60 Hz source with amp -0.6 added to the Add block. Result V6 pass. (c) hum_amp0_cut60.grc: hum amplitude set to 0 and hum_cutoff=60, the same cutoff as the 'cutoff 60' mutant that the oracle otherwise kills. Result V6 pass. Through all three the f2p check (band_fraction) passes trivially. The author knew about the zeroed or deleted hum source, but wrote it down only in the build.py docstring. Nothing in task.json (review.notes is empty) tells reviewers, and the author missed that the fault itself can be skipped entirely. The instruction says 'keep the File Sink' but does not say to keep the sources or the Add block (compare test-10, which lists what must be kept).
findings.suggested_fix: Preferred: add a second observation point on the unfiltered mix in the start, reference and variants. For example, a File Sink 'hummy.dat' (float) fed by the Add block, plus p2p checks on it: band_fraction 0-200 Hz ≈ 0.69 (hum power 0.18 of 0.26) and rms ≈ 0.51. State this in the instruction. That makes 6 functional blocks with filtering, so the item becomes L2. Re-check signature_split, because succ[] in compose.signature changes when the Add block has two outputs. Alternative: keep L1 and add 'Keep the two Signal Sources and the Add block as they are' to the instruction, and copy the known limitation into task.json review.notes so the team decides with the evidence in front of them.

findings.claim: The pass/fail boundary for the cutoff lies inside the High Pass Filter's nominal stopband, and the build.py docstring explains the failures wrongly. It says '80-110 Hz fail (60 Hz lies in the transition band)'. In fact designs with 60 Hz inside GRC's nominal stopband (cutoff - width/2) also fail. The reason is that firdes' Hamming tap-count heuristic delivers a transition band wider than the nominal width. These rejections are correct against the stated 0.1 % bound, but this GNU Radio-specific trap is what decides the borderline cases, and the item's documentation does not say so.
findings.evidence: cut115_w100.grc: nominal stopband edge 65 Hz, so 60 Hz is inside the stopband. Fails V6 with band_fraction 0.001462 > 0.001. cut150_w200.grc: nominal stopband edge 50 Hz. Fails with band_fraction 0.007997 and max_abs 0.4358 > 0.42. Direct firdes.high_pass(1,8000,c,w,WIN_HAMMING) response at 60 Hz: c=110/w=100 gives -27.7 dB; 115/100 gives -31.9 dB; 120/100 gives -37.0 dB; 150/200 gives -24.5 dB (97 taps). The bound needs about -33.5 dB at 60 Hz. cut120_w100 passes with band_fraction 0.000446.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the build.py docstring: failures extend into the nominal stopband, roughly while 60 Hz is less than about 10-15 Hz below cutoff - width/2 with Hamming. Record this boundary in review.notes so the team can decide whether the 0.1 % bound (about 30 dB) is intended. Relaxing it to, say, 1 % would still kill all 9 mutants (cutoff 60, bypass and rewire leave tens of percent of the power below 200 Hz), but tightening or keeping it is a team choice. The oracle is not wrong as written.

findings.claim: The chain-signature split does not keep this item's functional template out of other splits. The item follows the stated rule (its reference signature hashes to dev), but two of its own correct solutions hash to train-side signatures and one to a test signature. A test item (gbf-test-05) is also essentially the same template: two summed tones, a high-pass removes the lower one, the upper tone's amplitude is kept, L1, File Sink. A training-side generator may therefore legally emit this exact hum remover using fir_filter_xxx or band_pass_filter, which would inflate dev screening on this item.
findings.evidence: compose.signature_split results: reference/v1 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_xx|high_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink' → dev. v2 '…|fir_filter_xxx|…' → train. v4 '…|band_pass_filter|…' → train. v3 '…|band_reject_filter|…' → test. Also '…|iir_filter_xxx|…' → train, and gbf-test-05 '…|fft_filter_xxx|…' → test. gbf-test-05's instruction is the same concept: a 1 kHz + 6 kHz sum, a high-pass between them, the 6 kHz amplitude kept within 5 %. The disjointness field covers only training specs and does not mention the near-twin.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the training-side generators also reject the signatures of every benchmark item's variants (not only the reference), or normalise filter block ids (high_pass_filter, fir_filter_xxx, fft_filter_xxx, band_*_filter, iir_filter_xxx) into one class before hashing. Note the dev-04 / test-05 template overlap in review.notes so dev-based tuning is not mistaken for independent evidence.

compliance.verdict: The bookkeeping holds up, but the oracle has a fixable gap, so I could not confirm the item as a fully correct benchmark item yet. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates and every gate passes. The new gates.json is identical to the author's: solvability 10/10, 331 tokens, 4 of 4 variants reach V6, start graph first fails at V3 as expected, 9 valid mutants all killed. Running build.py in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-04 reproduces task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all four variants byte for byte. The split is correct: the signature hashes to dev. Licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false), fault, id/dir/split and level L1 (5 functional blocks) all match the rules. The canary appears only in task.json. Every mutation breaks a stated property and reaches V5. Tolerances follow the spec (1 % on frequency, 5 % on amplitude, the stated 0.1 % band limit), not run-to-run noise. The disjointness claims against reports/reference/training_task_specs.json are accurate. The instruction is clear and fair: obvious guesses fail for stated reasons (hum_cutoff 100 with width 100 gives 1.7 % of the power below 200 Hz), while cutoffs from 120 to 450 Hz, the four variants and a 6th-order Butterworth IIR answer all pass. The main finding (F1, medium): the requirement to filter the hum is not checked, and an answer that wires the tone straight to dehummed.dat (deleting the hum source, the Add and the faulty filter, never fixing the undefined name) passes V6. This can be fixed within L1 with an "edge" observation point on the Add block plus a sentence in the instruction. F2 to F4 are low: a template twin of test item gbf-test-05, tolerances not stated in the instruction, and mislabelled f2p/p2p groups. Probe scripts are in the session scratchpad folder rev04 (probe.py, probe2.py, probe3.py).

findings.claim: The oracle never checks the item's central requirement that the hum is still simulated and is removed by filtering. Two shortcut answers pass V6, and one of them never repairs the undefined variable. The author says this cannot be fixed within L1. That is wrong: the ladder already supports observation points that tap a block's output ("edge" points) and add no block.
findings.evidence: Probes run through ladder.check with the task's own task.json (scratch scripts probe.py and probe2.py). (a) Reference with the 60 Hz source's amp set to 0 reaches V6 (peak_freq 500, rms 0.282653, max_abs 0.399732, band_fraction 0.0). (b) tone_only reaches V6 (rms 0.282843, max_abs 0.4, band_fraction 0.0). tone_only is the start graph with the hum source, the Add and the High Pass Filter deleted, so the Signal Source feeds dehummed.dat directly. It is 3 blocks and the undefined name hum_cutoff disappears with the deleted filter. The instruction only requires "keep the File Sink" and "produces this output", so (b) arguably satisfies its literal wording. In that case the item does not measure the undefined_variable repair at all. Side note: build.py's claim that deleting the hum source alone passes is inaccurate. Removing it and setting the Add to num_inputs 1 fails V3. The author's stated reason for not fixing this ("a second observation point ... adds a 6th functional block, which is outside L1") is wrong. _worker._resolve_points supports {"name":..., "edge":{"block":..., "port":...}} points, which tap a block output with no extra block. probe2.py added edge point "mix" on blocks_add_xx_0 with a band_fraction check (50-70 Hz, min 0.6): the reference gives 0.692 and passes; zero-hum gives 0.0 and fails; tone_only fails ("block 'blocks_add_xx_0' not found"). Do not copy the start-up max_abs check used by gbf-test-05: a valid 6th-order Butterworth IIR high-pass (iir_filter_xxx, type ffd, scipy taps) passes the current oracle, but its start-up max_abs is 0.684, above 0.25, so that check would wrongly reject it (probe3.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the instruction such as: "Keep the two Signal Sources (the 500 Hz tone, amplitude 0.4, and the 60 Hz hum, amplitude 0.6) and the Add block blocks_add_xx_0 that mixes them as they are." Add an edge observation point on blocks_add_xx_0 port 0 with a p2p check that the mix still carries the hum. The bound comes from the stated numbers: 60 Hz power share 0.18/0.26 = 0.69, so use e.g. band_fraction 50-70 Hz, min 0.6. Rename the Add block in the variants to blocks_add_xx_0. Add the mutations "hum amp 0" and "tone wired straight to the File Sink". If the team prefers not to constrain block names, at least correct the rationale in the build.py docstring and author report, and record the accepted shortcut in review.notes.

findings.claim: Dev item gbf-dev-04 is a template twin of a test item's accepted solution (gbf-test-05). The signature-hash split rule is met in letter but does not separate the two.
findings.evidence: gbf-test-05 is a test build L1 item: 1 kHz and 6 kHz tones are added, a high-pass filter removes the lower tone, the upper tone keeps its amplitude within 5 %, and the output goes to a float File Sink. Its variants/v1_high_pass_filter_block.grc has exactly gbf-dev-04's chain: analog_sig_source_x x2, blocks_add_xx, high_pass_filter, blocks_file_sink. That is the same signature, which hashes to dev. The oracle features are the same too (peak_freq, rms, band_fraction). gbf-test-05 hashes to test only because its reference uses fft_filter_xxx. A correct repair of gbf-dev-04 is therefore a correctly parameterised solution of gbf-test-05. The eval plan uses the dev split for every choice, including checkpoint selection and the CI gate, so this narrows the dev/test separation. The disjointness field compares only against training-side specs and does not mention this twin.
findings.suggested_fix: Either change gbf-dev-04's scenario so it is not the same two-tone high-pass template, e.g. remove high-frequency interference with a low-pass filter or use a different topology, then re-check that signature_split is still dev. Or keep it and record the twin with gbf-test-05 in review.notes or disjointness so the team decides explicitly.

findings.claim: The instruction says the tone's peak amplitude 0.4 stays "unchanged" and does not state the tolerances the oracle applies (±5 % on amplitude, ±5 Hz on frequency). The oracle accepts a tone attenuated by about 4 %.
findings.evidence: Probe cutoff_450 (hum_cutoff = 450, width 100) passes V6 with rms 0.27144 (-4.0 %) and max_abs 0.383956 (-4.0 %), so a visibly attenuated tone counts as "unchanged". Sibling items state their tolerances: gbf-test-05 says "(0.5, within 5%)" and gbf-test-20 says "within 1 %" and "within 5 %". The authoring rule says every number the oracle depends on is stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Write e.g. "the 500 Hz tone (within 1 %) with its peak amplitude of 0.4 unchanged (within 5 %; an RMS of about 0.283)".

findings.claim: The fail-to-pass / pass-to-pass groups are mislabelled. The amplitude checks (rms, max_abs) are marked p2p, but the amplitude depends on the repaired cutoff value. The start graph does not run, so nothing "held in the starting flowgraph", which is how oracles.py defines p2p.
findings.evidence: In task.json, rms and max_abs are in group p2p. Wrong repairs break exactly these checks: cutoff_460 fails rms and max_abs, cutoff_110 fails max_abs (0.4248), and the mutation "hum_cutoff value 700" breaks the amplitude property. The start graph fails at V3, so no check can pass there. The sibling repair item gbf-test-08, written from the same template, labels rms and max_abs as f2p. No code under src/grcbench reads the group labels outside oracles.evaluate, so scoring is unaffected and the impact is limited to reporting and the team's reading of the item.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel the rms and max_abs checks as f2p, as gbf-test-08 does, keeping peak_freq as p2p. Or document the convention used for repair items whose start graph cannot run.
